verdict.rationale: USCIS publishes a first-party system-to-system channel, the Torch developer platform. It offers a Case Status API and a FOIA/PA request API that can create requests and check their status, with a published enrollment path: register a developer account, form a team, build in the sandbox, pass a demo, then receive production keys. The rail is narrow, though: the evidence states there is no filing API, so core form filing remains a human-account (myUSCIS) workflow. Missing for 10: machine submission of immigration forms and fees, broader transactional API coverage, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the Torch onboarding flow.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, a documented system-to-system channel exists for software to transact with the service (system accounts, transmitter programs, batch providers), with the enrollment path published

citations.quote: Complete the onboarding task to register for a USCIS Torch API Developer account. ... Create a developer team or join an existing team.
Gain Access and develop in our Sandbox environment to send test data.
Pass the demo and receive production keys to launch your application.
This API allows consumers to create a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) or Privacy Act (PA) request, for Alien File material, about or on behalf of the subject of record.
Provides case status information to USCIS customers and their representatives who require regular access to case status information.
There is no filing API; myUSCIS is the only online filing rail.
